basis: 2026-09-17 reviewed MCP economy and reliability contract: public tools keep session/state IDs, delta hashes, native action IDs, combat decision tokens, required fixed map_id/revision, and event reading_id server-side; JSON payloads are single-copy and auto-TOON when losslessly smaller; normal transport/success/mechanics audit metadata and narrative observer bookkeeping are omitted; hand TOC carries current cost; multi-card reads share an inline budget; equivalent hand copies collapse only when complete observed state differs solely by identity/hand-index/render provenance; exact physical refs remain available through context. Only required const/single-enum action parameters are stripped from public schemas/examples and restored from the exact pinned native action before dispatch, preserving optional-parameter semantics. Public required arguments are checked in the MCP server before dispatch, so missing commentary/target/route arguments cannot consume the bridge single-flight slot. Game-side terminal action errors preserve the original request_id, and McpBridge additionally attributes an uncorrelated terminal result/error to its sole pending request, so rejected actions cannot permanently return busy_outcome_pending. Post-action play control does not re-arm an unchanged decision, and offered action-set changes participate in decision identity to prevent stale reward/selection actions from surviving transitions. Ordinary copied-profile event actions are wired through RunUi/MenuControlSession/ProtocolSession; this is not a claim that every Downfall custom event/minigame/selector has live-game acceptance. Default combat decisions now preserve compact current player and monster powers (localized name, BUFF/DEBUFF type when available, stack amount, short public description and select visible values) while omitting raw power IDs; full power objects remain available through player/powers and monsters/N/powers refs, and size fallback drops power descriptions before dropping the power identity itself.
